A generalized character related to the pp-local structure and representation theory of a finite group

Geoffrey R. Robinson Affiliation: Institute of Mathematics Affiliation: University of Aberdeen Affiliation: Fraser Noble Building Affiliation: Aberdeen Affiliation: AB24 3UE Affiliation: United Kingdom
Abstract

Let GG be a finite group and pp be a prime. Let (𝕂,R,𝔽)(\mathbb{K},R,\mathbb{F}) be a (splitting) pp-modular system for GG.

We let GpG_{p} denote the set of pp-elements of GG and Gp′G_{p^{\prime}} denote the set of pp-regular elements of GG. In this note, we examine the generalized character Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} of GG which vanishes on all pp-singular elements and whose value at each pp-regular y∈Gy\in G is the number of pp-elements of CG​(y).C_{G}(y). We examine cases when Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character, and when it is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module. We conjecture that, in fact, Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is always a character, and may always be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module. We discuss some properties of Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G}, and relate it to a truncated version of the R​GRG-module afforded by the conjugation action of GG on itself.

Since the virtual character Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} vanishes on pp-singular elements, it corresponds to a unique virtual projective module P1,p,GP_{1,p,G} in the Green ring for R​GRG, and we obtain a uniform explicit expression for P1,p,GP_{1,p,G} which is valid for all finite GG. It is however not immediately obvious from this expression whether or not P1,p,GP_{1,p,G} is always a module. On the other hand, letting RR denote the trivial R​GRG-module, we give a general explicit formula expressing P1,p,G−RP_{1,p,G}-R (in the Green ring for R​GRG) as a virtual module induced from (proper) pp-local subgroups of GG when Op​(G)=1.O_{p}(G)=1.

Among other examples, we prove for each prime pp and each prime power qq (not necessarily divisible by pp) that P1,p,GP_{1,p,G} is a genuine projective R​GRG-module when G≅PSL⁡(2,q)G\cong{\rm PSL}(2,q) and when G≅SL⁡(2,q).G\cong{\rm SL}(2,q).

To the memory of Marty Isaacs

1 Notation and Introduction

Let GG be a finite group, pp be a prime, (𝕂,R,𝔽)(\mathbb{K},R,\mathbb{F}) be a (splitting) pp-modular system for GG.

When nn is a positive integer and π\pi is a set of primes, we let nπn_{\pi} denote the largest positive integer which divides nn and is itself only divisible by primes in π.\pi. As usual, when g∈Gg\in G and π\pi is a set of primes, we may (uniquely) write g=x​y=y​xg=xy=yx with ⟨x⟩\langle x\rangle a π\pi-group and ⟨y⟩\langle y\rangle a π′\pi^{\prime}-group. We call xx the π\pi-part of gg and denote it by gπ.g_{\pi}. The π\pi-section of g∈Gg\in G is the set of elements of GG whose π\pi-part is conjugate to gπg_{\pi}, and is denoted by SπG​(g){\rm S}_{\pi}^{G}(g) (usually we will take gg to be a π\pi-element itself). The element g∈Gg\in G is said to be π\pi-singular if gπ≠1Gg_{\pi}\neq 1_{G}, and π\pi-regular otherwise.

We let GpG_{p} denote the set of pp-elements of GG and Gp′G_{p^{\prime}} denote the set of pp-regular elements of GG. Let {ϕi:1≤i≤ℓ}\{\phi_{i}:1\leq i\leq\ell\} be the irreducible Brauer characters of GG, and let {θi:1≤i≤ℓ}\{\theta_{i}:1\leq i\leq\ell\} be the set of characters of the projective indecomposable R​GRG-modules, where we label so that ⟨θi,ϕj⟩=δi​j\langle\theta_{i},\phi_{j}\rangle=\delta_{ij} for 1≤i,j≤ℓ.1\leq i,j\leq\ell. (When α\alpha is a class function which is only defined for pp-regular elements and β\beta is a class function of GG which vanishes on pp-singular elements, we will use ⟨α,β⟩\langle\alpha,\beta\rangle to denote

1|G|​(∑g∈Gp′α​(g)​β⁡(g)¯),\frac{1}{|G|}\left(\sum_{g\in G_{p^{\prime}}}\alpha(g)\overline{\beta(g)}\right),

which is compatible with the usual notation for the standard inner product on class functions of GG).

We define the class function Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} of GG to take value 00 on all pp-singular elements of GG, and to take value

Ψ1,p,G​(y)=\Psi_{1,p,G}(y)= (the number of pp-elements of CG​(y)C_{G}(y)) whenever y∈Gy\in G is pp-regular.

Notice that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} agrees with the permutation character

∑x∈Gp/GIndCG​(x)G​(1)\sum_{x\in G_{p}/G}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(x)}^{G}(1)

on pp-regular elements (and vanishes elsewhere). We note also that it is clear that algebraically conjugate irreducible characters occur with equal multiplicity in Ψ1,p,G.\Psi_{1,p,G}.

By a well-known theorem of Frobenius, we know that |CG​(y)|p|C_{G}(y)|_{p} divides |CG​(y)p||C_{G}(y)_{p}| for each pp-regular y∈Gy\in G. By Brauer’s characterization of characters, it follows that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a generalized character of GG.

To see that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a generalized character, notice that whenever EE is a Brauer elementary subgroup of GG of order prime to pp, the class function ResEG​(Ψ1,p,G){\rm Res}^{G}_{E}(\Psi_{1,p,G}) is a character of EE (since it agrees with the restriction to EE of a permutation character). If a Brauer elementary subgroup EE has the form P×FP\times F for some non-trivial pp-group PP and some p′p^{\prime}-group FF, then

ResEG​(Ψ1,p,G)=IndFE​(ResFG​(Ψ1,p,G)|P|){\rm Res}^{G}_{E}(\Psi_{1,p,G})={\rm Ind}_{F}^{E}(\frac{{\rm Res}^{G}_{F}(\Psi_{1,p,G})}{|P|})

and

ResFG​(Ψ1,p,G)|P|\frac{{\rm Res}^{G}_{F}(\Psi_{1,p,G})}{|P|}

is a character of F.F. Using Brauer’s induction theorem, it also follows that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-linear combination of characters each induced from linear characters of Brauer elementary p′p^{\prime}-subgroups of G.G.

Since Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} agrees with a character on pp-regular elements, and each (irreducible character χ\chi in a) pp-block of defect zero of GG vanishes off pp-regular elements, it follows that ⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle is a non-negative integer whenever χ\chi is (an irreducible character in) a pp-block of defect zero of GG. In fact, we have

⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩=∑x∈Gp/G⟨ResCG​(x)G​(χ),1⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle=\sum_{x\in G_{p}/G}\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{C_{G}(x)}(\chi),1\rangle

for each such χ.\chi.

Notice that if x∈Gpx\in G_{p} and zpk=xz^{p^{k}}=x, we have CG​(z)≤CG​(x)C_{G}(z)\leq C_{G}(x), and that, furthermore, two such pkp^{k}-th roots of xx which are conjugate in GG are already conjugate in CG​(x).C_{G}(x).

Now if ⟨ResCG​(x)G​(χ),1⟩>0\langle{\rm Res}_{C_{G}(x)}^{G}(\chi),1\rangle>0 we must have ⟨ResCG​(z)G​(χ),1⟩>0\langle{\rm Res}_{C_{G}(z)}^{G}(\chi),1\rangle>0 for any such zz. It follows by Frobenius reciprocity that ⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle is at least as great as the number of CG​(x)C_{G}(x)-conjugacy classes of pp-power roots of xx when such an xx exists.

In the case p=2,p=2, whenever χ\chi is a real-valued irreducible character in a 22-block of defect zero of GG, there is (by Theorem 8 of Murray [12]) an involution
t∈Gt\in G, unique up to conjugacy, such that ⟨χ,IndCG​(t)G​(1)⟩>0,\langle\chi,{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(t)}^{G}(1)\rangle>0, and the multiplicity is in fact 11. Hence the above argument shows that ⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle is at least as great as the number of CG​(t)C_{G}(t)-conjugacy classes of 22-power roots of tt (including tt itself).

2 The generalized character Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} and root counting

Notice that if GG has a Sylow pp-subgroup SS, then Ψ1,p,G​(x)\Psi_{1,p,G}(x) is the number of |S||S|-th roots of xx in GG. If xx is pp-singular, there is clearly no such root of xx, while if xx is pp-regular and y|S|=x,y^{|S|}=x, then yy has the form u​v=v​uuv=vu where uu is the unique generator of ⟨x⟩\langle x\rangle with u|S|=xu^{|S|}=x and vv is a pp-element of CG​(x).C_{G}(x). In fact, we may choose a power qq of pp so that |S||S| divides qq and q≡1q\equiv 1 (mod |G|p′|G|_{p^{\prime}}), and then we see easily that Ψ1,p,G​(x)\Psi_{1,p,G}(x) is the number of qq-th roots of xx in GG for each x∈Gx\in G.

Now for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG, it is well-known that the class function χ(q)\chi^{(q)} of GG defined by χ(q)​(g)=χ⁡(gq)\chi^{(q)}(g)=\chi(g^{q}) for all g∈Gg\in G is a generalized character of GG. Note that we have χ(q)​(g)=χ⁡(gp′)\chi^{(q)}(g)=\chi(g_{p^{\prime}}) for each gg by the choice of qq.

Setting νq​(χ)=⟨χ(q),1⟩,\nu_{q}(\chi)=\langle\chi^{(q)},1\rangle, we see easily that

Ψ1,p,G=∑χ∈Irr⁡(G)νq​(χ)​χ,\Psi_{1,p,G}=\sum_{\chi\in{\rm Irr}(G)}\nu_{q}(\chi)\chi,

so that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character of GG if and only if νq​(χ)≥0\nu_{q}(\chi)\geq 0 for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG.

We may note further that νq​(χ)≤χ⁡(1)\nu_{q}(\chi)\leq\chi(1) with equality if and only if

χ⁡(gp′)=χ⁡(1)\chi(g_{p^{\prime}})=\chi(1)

for all g∈G,g\in G, so that νq​(χ)=χ​(1)\nu_{q}(\chi)=\chi(1) if and only if Op​(G)≤ker​χ.O^{p}(G)\leq{\rm ker}\chi.

We also note that

−χ⁡(1)<νq​(χ)≤χ⁡(1)-\chi(1)<\nu_{q}(\chi)\leq\chi(1)

for each irreducible character χ\chi of G,G, so that when χ\chi is linear, we have νq​(χ)≥0\nu_{q}(\chi)\geq 0 and νq​(χ)=1=χ⁡(1)\nu_{q}(\chi)=1=\chi(1) if and only if Op​(G)≤ker​χ.O^{p}(G)\leq{\rm ker}\chi. Hence we have proved:

Theorem 2.1: We have G≠Op​(G)G\neq O^{p}(G) if and only if Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} contains some non-trivial linear character with non-zero multiplicity. Furthermore, for every irreducible character χ\chi of GG, we have

−χ⁡(1)<νq​(χ)≤χ⁡(1),-\chi(1)<\nu_{q}(\chi)\leq\chi(1),

and the irreducible characters χ\chi of GG which occur with multiplicity χ⁡(1)\chi(1) in Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} are precisely the irreducible characters of GG with Op​(G)O^{p}(G) in their kernels.

Another extreme case is:

Theorem 2.2: Let χ\chi be an irreducible character of GG such that

Op′​(G)≤ker​χ.O^{p^{\prime}}(G)\leq{\rm ker}\chi.

Then χ\chi occurs with zero multiplicity in Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} except when χ\chi is the trivial character, in which case, χ\chi occurs with multiplicity one in Ψ1,p,G.\Psi_{1,p,G}. In any case, χ\chi occurs with non-negative multiplicity in Ψ1,p,G.\Psi_{1,p,G}.

Proof: The given hypothesis on χ\chi is equivalent to asserting that every pp-element of GG lies in ker​χ.{\rm ker}\chi. Hence for each g∈G,g\in G, we have χ(q)​(g)=χ⁡(gp′)=χ⁡(g).\chi^{(q)}(g)=\chi(g_{p^{\prime}})=\chi(g). Thus χ(q)=χ\chi^{(q)}=\chi, so that νq​(χ)=δ1,χ\nu_{q}(\chi)=\delta_{1,\chi} and the result follows.

Remark 2.3: Note that Theorem 2.1 implies, in particular that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the regular character of GG if and only if GG is a pp-group. On the other hand, if GG is a p′p^{\prime}-group, then Theorem 2.2 implies that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the trivial character. Finally, we note that if Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the trivial character, then GG contains only one pp-element, so that (by Cauchy’s theorem), GG is a p′p^{\prime}-group.

Hence we have:

Corollary 2.4: Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the trivial character if and only if GG is a p′p^{\prime}-group. Also, Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the regular character if and only if GG is a pp-group.

Remark 2.5: In the case of symmetric groups, generalized characters which count the numbers of roots of a given element are well-understood. T. Scharf has proved in [15] that for any two positive integers mm and nn, the integer-valued class function θm\theta_{m} of the symmetric group SnS_{n} defined by letting θm​(x)\theta_{m}(x) denote the number of mm-th roots of xx in SnS_{n} is a character of Sn.S_{n}. No such result is true for the general finite group GG. Notice that Scharf’s result implies, in particular, that Ψ1,p,Sn\Psi_{1,p,S_{n}} is a character of SnS_{n} for every prime pp and every positive integer nn.

3 Some general observations

Remark 3.1: For a general finite group GG, we note that

⟨Ψ1,p,G,1⟩=1|G|​(∑y∈Gp′/G|Sp′G​(y)|)=1,\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},1\rangle=\frac{1}{|G|}\left(\sum_{y\in G_{p^{\prime}}/G}|S_{p^{\prime}}^{G}(y)|\right)=1,

since for each pp-regular y∈G,y\in G, the cardinality of the p′p^{\prime}-section of yy in GG is

[G:CG(y)][G:C_{G}(y)] ×\times (the number of pp-elements of CG​(y)C_{G}(y)).

Hence, by block orthogonality relations, the character of the projective cover of the trivial module occurs exactly once when Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is uniquely expressed as a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-linear combination of characters of projective indecomposable R​GRG-modules.

In this note, we are principally concerned with two questions: firstly, is Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} always a character? Secondly, is Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} a non-negative integer combination of characters of projective indecomposable R​GRG-modules (which certainly would imply that it is a character)? We conjecture that the latter is always the case. Though we are not able to prove this at present, we illustrate that it is true in many cases, and we draw some consequences for groups such that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

We now note the following extension of Corollary 2.4:

Theorem 3.2 : i) Suppose that GG has a normal pp-complement. Then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character, and may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

ii) Suppose that GG has a normal Sylow pp-subgroup. Then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the character afforded by the projective cover of the trivial R​GRG-module.

iii) If Ψ1,p,G/Op​(G)\Psi_{1,p,G/O_{p}(G)} is a character of G/Op​(G)G/O_{p}(G) afforded by a projective R​G/Op​(G)RG/O_{p}(G)-module MM, then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is afforded by P⁡(M),P(M), the projective cover (as R​GRG-module) of the inflation of MM to an R​GRG-module.

Proof: i) It suffices to prove that whenever ϕi\phi_{i} is a Brauer irreducible character of GG, then

⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi⟩≥0.\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}\rangle\geq 0.

But

⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi⟩=∑x∈Gp/G⟨ResCG​(x)G​(ϕi),1⟩′≥0,\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}\rangle=\sum_{x\in G_{p}/G}\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{C_{G}(x)}(\phi_{i}),1\rangle^{\prime}\geq 0,

where ⟨,⟩′\langle,\rangle^{\prime} denotes that the inner product is restricted to pp-regular elements.

For each pp-element x∈Gx\in G, the set of pp-regular elements of CG​(x)C_{G}(x) is the subgroup Op′​(CG​(x))O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x)), and it follows that

|CG​(x)|p​⟨ResCG​(x)G​(ϕi),1⟩′|C_{G}(x)|_{p}\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{C_{G}(x)}(\phi_{i}),1\rangle^{\prime}

is a non-negative integer, and, in particular, ⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}\rangle is non-negative, since ϕi\phi_{i} always restricts to a character of Op′​(CG​(x))O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x)) (and we already know that the inner product in question is an integer).

To be precise, we have

Ψ1,p,G=∑i=1ℓ(∑x∈Gp/G⟨ResOp′​(CG​(x))G​(ϕi),1⟩|CG​(x)|p)​θi.\Psi_{1,p,G}=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\left(\sum_{x\in G_{p}/G}\frac{\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x))}(\phi_{i}),1\rangle}{|C_{G}(x)|_{p}}\right)\theta_{i}.

ii) Suppose that GG has a normal Sylow pp-subgroup PP. Then GG has a Hall p′p^{\prime}-subgroup HH, and the character IndHG​(1){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1) is easily seen to take value |CP​(y)||C_{P}(y)| for each y∈Hy\in H. But for each such yy, the subgroup CG​(y)C_{G}(y) has a normal Sylow pp-subgroup CP​(y)C_{P}(y) and we have |CP​(y)|=|CG​(y)p|=Ψ1,p,G​(y).|C_{P}(y)|=|C_{G}(y)_{p}|=\Psi_{1,p,G}(y). Hence

Ψ1,p,G=IndHG​(1),\Psi_{1,p,G}={\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1),

which is the character afforded by the projective cover of the trivial module.

iii) A theorem of W.F. Reynolds [13] asserts that if HH is a finite group and
U=Op​(H)U=O_{p}(H), then whenever α\alpha is the Brauer character of a projective
R​H/URH/U-module XX and β\beta is the Brauer character afforded by the projective cover of XX as R​HRH-module, then for each pp-regular y∈H,y\in H, we have

β⁡(y)=|CU​(y)|​α​(y​U)\beta(y)=|C_{U}(y)|\alpha(yU)

for all pp-regular y∈Hy\in H. In fact, Reynolds’ observation gives a (Brauer character preserving) bijection between virtual Brauer characters of virtual projective R​H/URH/U-modules and virtual Brauer characters of virtual projective R​HRH-modules, obtained by multiplying the virtual projective Brauer character of H/UH/U by the Brauer character afforded by the conjugation action of HH on UU.

Remark 3.3 : Theorem 3.2 tells us that if GG has a normal pp-complement or a normal Sylow pp-subgroup, or if Ψ1,p,G/Op​(G)\Psi_{1,p,G/O_{p}(G)} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module, then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module. It follows that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module if G=Op,p′,p​(G).G=O_{p,p^{\prime},p}(G).

By P. Fong’s theorems on characters of pp-solvable groups (see [7]), it is known that when GG is pp-solvable, a character which vanishes on pp-singular elements may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module. Hence to prove for such GG that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character which may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module, it is sufficient to prove that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character of GG.

4 The generalized character Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} and blocks of R​GRG

Since Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a virtual projective character of GG, it may be uniquely decomposed as an orthogonal sum ∑bΨ1,p,G(b)\sum_{b}\Psi^{(b)}_{1,p,G} where bb runs over the blocks of R​GRG, and each Ψ1,p,G(b)\Psi^{(b)}_{1,p,G} is a (possibly zero) virtual projective character which is a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-linear combination of irreducible characters in bb.

Generalizing some of the results of the previous section, we may note that:

Theorem 4.1: If bb is a block of R​GRG, then Ψ1,p,G(b)\Psi^{(b)}_{1,p,G} contains the character of at least one projective indecomposable bb-module with non-negative multiplicity. In particular, if ℓ⁡(b)=1,\ell(b)=1, then Ψ1,p,G(b)\Psi^{(b)}_{1,p,G} is either zero or else is a character of GG which may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

Proof: Let θi\theta_{i} be the character afforded by some projective indecomposable bb-module. Then

⟨θi,Ψ1,p,G⟩≥0,\langle\theta_{i},\Psi_{1,p,G}\rangle\geq 0,

since θi\theta_{i} vanishes on all pp-singular elements and Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} agrees with a permutation character on pp-regular elements.

Now θi\theta_{i} agrees with a non-negative integer linear combination of Brauer irreducible characters in bb on pp-regular elements. Hence there must be some jj with

⟨ϕj,Ψ1,p,G⟩≥0\langle\phi_{j},\Psi_{1,p,G}\rangle\geq 0

(and with ϕj∈b\phi_{j}\in b). Then the character θj\theta_{j} is a character of a projective indecomposable bb-module, and occurs with non-negative multiplicity when Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is expressed as a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-linear combination of {θr:1≤r≤ℓ}.\{\theta_{r}:1\leq r\leq\ell\}.

Remark 4.2 : This provides an alternative proof of part i) of Theorem 3.2. It also reproves the fact that irreducible characters in pp-blocks of defect zero all occur with non-negative multiplicity in Ψ1,p,G.\Psi_{1,p,G}.

5 Other p′p^{\prime}-sections

Let yy be a pp-regular element of GG, and consider the generalized character Ψ1,p,CG​(y)\Psi_{1,p,C_{G}(y)} of CG​(y),C_{G}(y), which vanishes on all pp-singular elements of CG​(y)C_{G}(y), and takes value (the number of pp-elements of CG​(y)∩CG​(z)C_{G}(y)\cap C_{G}(z)) for each pp-regular zz in CG​(y)C_{G}(y). This is the exact analogue of Ψ1,p,G,\Psi_{1,p,G}, but for the subgroup CG​(y)C_{G}(y).

Then Ψ1,p,CG​(y)\Psi_{1,p,C_{G}(y)} agrees with

∑x∈CG​(y)p/CG​(y)IndCG​(x​y)CG​(y)​(1)\sum_{x\in C_{G}(y)_{p}/C_{G}(y)}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(xy)}^{C_{G}(y)}(1)

on pp-regular elements of CG​(y)C_{G}(y) and vanishes on all pp-singular elements of CG​(y)C_{G}(y). Notice then that IndCG​(y)G​(Ψ1,p,CG​(y)){\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(y)}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,C_{G}(y)}) agrees on pp-regular elements of GG with the character afforded by the conjugation action of GG on the p′p^{\prime}-section of y,y, and vanishes on all pp-singular elements of GG.

Hence we see that

∑y∈Gp′/GIndCG​(y)G​(Ψ1,p,CG​(y))\sum_{y\in G_{p^{\prime}}/G}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(y)}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,C_{G}(y)})

agrees on pp-regular elements of GG with the character afforded by the conjugation action of GG on itself, and vanishes on all pp-singular elements of GG. Thus, by block orthogonality relations, we have:

Remark 5.1:

∑y∈Gp′/GIndCG​(y)G​(Ψ1,p,CG​(y))=∑i=1ℓϕi¯​θi.\sum_{y\in G_{p^{\prime}}/G}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(y)}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,C_{G}(y)})=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\overline{\phi_{i}}\theta_{i}.

We call this character the truncated conjugation character of G, and denote it by Λc,p,G\Lambda_{c,p,G}. We denote the projective R​GRG-module affording this character by Tc,p,GT_{c,p,G} and call it the truncated conjugation module.

Note that Λc,p,G\Lambda_{c,p,G} takes value |CG​(y)||C_{G}(y)| on each pp-regular element y∈Gy\in G (and vanishes on all pp-singular elements). Note also that Tc,p,GT_{c,p,G} is the lift to an R​GRG-module of the projective 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-module ⨁SHom⁡(S,P⁡(S)),\bigoplus_{S}{\rm Hom}(S,P(S)), where SS runs over a full set of isomorphism types of absolutely irreducible 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-modules, and P⁡(S)P(S) denotes the projective cover of SS as 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-module.

We remark that the multiplicity of the projective cover of the trivial module as a summand of the 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-module ⨁SHom⁡(S,P⁡(S)),\bigoplus_{S}{\rm Hom}(S,P(S)), is ℓ⁡(G),\ell(G), the number of simple 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-modules, which is also the number of pp-regular conjugacy classes of GG.

We note that if ZZ is a central p′p^{\prime}-subgroup of GG, then for each pp-regular y∈Gy\in G, the number of pp-elements in CG​(y)C_{G}(y) is the same as the number of pp-elements of CG/Z​(y​Z).C_{G/Z}(yZ). For if xx is a pp-element of GG with [y,x]∈y​Z,[y,x]\in yZ, then we have x∈CG​(y)x\in C_{G}(y) by a standard argument, and xx is the unique pp-element in x​Z.xZ. Hence Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the inflation to GG of Ψ1,p,G/Z\Psi_{1,p,G/Z}, and Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is afforded by a projective module if and only if Ψ1,p,G/Z\Psi_{1,p,G/Z} is afforded by a projective module.

Hence to prove that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is afforded by a projective R​GRG-module, we may assume by induction that Z⁡(G)Z(G) is a pp-group. But we have already dealt with the case Op​(G)≠1,O_{p}(G)\neq 1, so to prove that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module, we may assume by induction that Op​(G)=Z⁡(G)=1.O_{p}(G)=Z(G)=1.

Example 5.2: If we consider the special case that G=GL⁡(n,pa)G={\rm GL}(n,p^{a}) for some positive integer aa, then for each pp-regular element y∈Gy\in G, it is clear (and well-known) that CG​(y)C_{G}(y) is a direct product of general linear groups over fields of characteristic pp (allowing the possibility that a cyclic group of order pr−1p^{r}-1 is considered as GL⁡(1,pr){\rm GL}(1,p^{r})). The Steinberg character St1{\rm St}_{1} of GG is known to have degree |G|p|G|_{p} and, more generally, to take value ±|CG​(y)|p\pm|C_{G}(y)|_{p} for each pp-regular y∈Gy\in G.

Hence, for each pp-regular y∈G,y\in G, we see that CG​(y)C_{G}(y) has a Steinberg character Sty{\rm St}_{y}, and we have St1​(y)=±Sty​(1){\rm St}_{1}(y)=\pm{\rm St}_{y}(1) for each pp-regular y∈Gy\in G. Since St1{\rm St}_{1} is irreducible and vanishes on pp-singular elements, we have

|G|=∑y∈Gp′/G[G:CG(y)]Sty(1)2.|G|=\sum_{y\in G_{p^{\prime}/G}}[G:C_{G}(y)]{\rm St}_{y}(1)^{2}.

Since we have
|G|=∑y∈Gp′/G[G:CG(y)]×|G|=\sum_{y\in G_{p^{\prime}/G}}[G:C_{G}(y)]\times (the number of pp-elements of 𝑂𝑃𝐸𝑁CG​(y))C_{G}(y)), an inductive argument recovers the well-known fact that for each pp-regular y∈Gy\in G, the number of pp-elements in CG​(y)C_{G}(y) is equal to |CG​(y)|p2|C_{G}(y)|_{p}^{2}.

Notice then that now we have Ψ1,p,G=St12,\Psi_{1,p,G}={\rm St}_{1}^{2}, so proving that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is afforded by a projective R​GRG-module, since the Steinberg character of GG is afforded by a projective R​GRG-module for this choice of GG.

In fact, the same statement holds whenever GG is a finite group which has a (split,restricted) B​NBN-pair with characteristic pp (the number of pp-elements of CG​(y)C_{G}(y) is equal to |CG​(y)|p2|C_{G}(y)|_{p}^{2} whenever y∈Gy\in G is pp-regular, and consequently Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is afforded by a projective R​GRG-module, for all such GG). We will provide a new proof of this result later.

Returning to the case G=GL⁡(n,pa)G={\rm GL}(n,p^{a}), we note that we have

Λc,p,G=∑y∈Gp′/GIndCG​(y)G​(Sty2).\Lambda_{c,p,G}=\sum_{y\in G_{p^{\prime}}/G}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(y)}^{G}({\rm St}_{y}^{2}).

6 Some consequences of non-negativity

When ϕ\phi is a Brauer character of GG (with respect to the prime pp), we define the generalized character ϕ∗\phi^{\ast} of GG via ϕ∗​(x​y)=ϕ​(y)\phi^{\ast}(xy)=\phi(y) whenever xx is a pp-element and yy is a pp-regular element with x​y=y​xxy=yx. That this is a generalized character of GG is an easy consequence of Brauer’s characterization of characters, as noted by J.A. Green in [8].

Theorem 6.1: Let GG be a finite group. Then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a non-negative integer combination of characters of projective indecomposable R​GRG-modules if and only if we have ⟨ϕi∗,ϕj∗⟩≥0\langle\phi_{i}^{\ast},\phi_{j}^{\ast}\rangle\geq 0 for 1≤i,j≤ℓ1\leq i,j\leq\ell.

Proof: Let ϕi\phi_{i} be an irreducible Brauer character of GG.

Then the coefficient of θi\theta_{i} when Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is expressed as a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-linear combination of characters of projective indecomposable R​GRG-modules is

⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi⟩=⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi∗⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}\rangle=\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}^{\ast}\rangle

(recall that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} vanishes on pp-singular elements, so on all elements of the p′p^{\prime}-section of yy outside the conjugacy class of yy).

Since Ψ1,p,G​(y)=\Psi_{1,p,G}(y)= (the number of pp-elements of CG​(y)C_{G}(y)) for each pp-regular y∈G,y\in G, we see from the definitions of Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} and ϕi∗\phi_{i}^{\ast} that this last inner product is ⟨1,ϕi∗⟩.\langle 1,\phi_{i}^{\ast}\rangle.

Hence Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module if and only if

⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi⟩=⟨1,ϕi∗⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}\rangle=\langle 1,\phi_{i}^{\ast}\rangle

is non-negative for each absolutely irreducible Brauer character ϕi\phi_{i} of GG. Suppose then that this positivity condition holds.

It is clear that if ϕi\phi_{i} and ϕj\phi_{j} are irreducible Brauer characters, then ϕi¯∗​ϕj∗\overline{\phi_{i}}^{\ast}\phi_{j}^{\ast} is a non-negative integer combination of extended (that is to say, starred) Brauer irreducible characters, so this implies that

⟨ϕi∗,ϕj∗⟩=⟨ϕi¯∗​ϕj∗,1⟩≥0.\langle\phi_{i}^{\ast},\phi_{j}^{\ast}\rangle=\langle\overline{\phi_{i}}^{\ast}\phi_{j}^{\ast},1\rangle\geq 0.

Hence if Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the character of a projective R​GRG-module, then

⟨ϕi∗,ϕj∗⟩≥0\langle\phi_{i}^{\ast},\phi_{j}^{\ast}\rangle\geq 0

for all i,ji,j.

On the other hand, if such inner products are always non-negative, then the case that ϕj\phi_{j} is the trivial character already implies that

⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi⟩=⟨1,ϕi∗⟩≥0\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}\rangle=\langle 1,\phi_{i}^{\ast}\rangle\geq 0

for each ii, so that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a non-negative integer combination of characters of projective indecomposable R​GRG-modules.

Remark 6.2 : Since the generalized characters ϕi∗\phi_{i}^{\ast} are not, in general, characters, this non-negativity condition appears to be slightly surprising.

7 Some remarks on Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} for groups in which the centralizer of each non-identity pp-element has a normal pp-complement

We suppose (throughout this section) that the centralizer of each non-identity pp-element of GG has a normal pp-complement.

We may decompose Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} according to blocks of R​GRG. We let B0B_{0} denote the principal block of R​GRG, and we set

Ψ1,p,G(0)=∑χ∈Irr⁡(B0)⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩​χ.\Psi^{(0)}_{1,p,G}=\sum_{\chi\in{\rm Irr}(B_{0})}\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle\chi.

Then we define Ψ1,p,G(1)\Psi^{(1)}_{1,p,G} as Ψ1,p,G−Ψ1,p,G(0).\Psi_{1,p,G}-\Psi^{(0)}_{1,p,G}.

Theorem 7.1: Ψ1,p,G(1)\Psi^{(1)}_{1,p,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

Proof: It suffices to prove that whenever ϕi\phi_{i} is an absolutely irreducible Brauer character in a non-principal block of R​GRG, then

⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi⟩≥0.\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}\rangle\geq 0.

We have

⟨Ψ1,p,G,ϕi⟩=∑x∈Gp/G⟨ResCG​(x)G​(ϕi),1⟩′\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\phi_{i}\rangle=\sum_{x\in G_{p}/G}\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{C_{G}(x)}(\phi_{i}),1\rangle^{\prime}

and (since CG​(x)C_{G}(x) has a normal pp-complement whenever 1≠x1\neq x is a pp-element) the contribution from non-identity pp-elements xx is non-negative.

But by block orthogonality relations, we know that ∑g∈Gp′ϕi​(g)=0\sum_{g\in G_{p^{\prime}}}\phi_{i}(g)=0 whenever ϕi\phi_{i} is a Brauer irreducible character not in the principal block of R​GRG, so the required non-negativity follows for all Brauer characters in non-principal blocks.

As a consequence of 7.1, we have:

Corollary 7.2 : Let GG be a finite group whose Sylow pp-subgroups are cyclic, dihedral or Klein four, or that GG has an Abelian Sylow pp-subgroup PP such that NG​(P)/Op′​(CG​(P))N_{G}(P)/O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(P)) is a Frobenius group with Frobenius kernel isomorphic to PP.

Then we may write Ψ1,p,G=Ψ1,p,G(0)+Ψ1,p,G(1),\Psi_{1,p,G}=\Psi^{(0)}_{1,p,G}+\Psi^{(1)}_{1,p,G}, where Ψ1,p,G(0)\Psi^{(0)}_{1,p,G} is a virtual projective character which is a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-combination of irreducible characters in the principal pp-block, and Ψ1,p,G(1)\Psi^{(1)}_{1,p,G} is the character of a projective R​GRG-module which has no indecomposable summand in the principal pp-block of GG.

Proof: In all of the cases listed, CG​(x)C_{G}(x) has a normal pp-complement for each non-identity pp-element x∈Gx\in G.

Theorem 7.3 Suppose that CG​(x)C_{G}(x) has a normal pp-complement for each non-identity pp-element x∈G.x\in G. Then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character of GG.

Proof: By 7.1, it suffices to prove that ⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩≥0\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle\geq 0 for each irreducible character χ\chi in the principal pp-block of GG. It is clearly sufficient to consider the case that χ\chi is non-trivial, since (for example), we always have ⟨Ψ1,p,G,1⟩=1.\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},1\rangle=1.

We first note that if χ\chi is a non-trivial irreducible character in the principal pp-block of GG, then we have ∑g∈Gχ⁡(g)=0,\sum_{g\in G}\chi(g)=0, and from this (and from Brauer’s Second and Third Main Theorems, since they imply that χ\chi is constant on non-identity pp-sections), we easily deduce that

1|G|(∑g∈Gp′χ(g))=−∑1≠x∈Gp/Gχ⁡(x)|CG​(x)|p.\frac{1}{|G|}\left(\sum_{g\in G_{p^{\prime}}}\chi(g)\right)=-\sum_{1\neq x\in G_{p}/G}\frac{\chi(x)}{|C_{G}(x)|_{p}}.

We may note as in the previous proofs that for each non-identity pp-element xx of GG, we have

1|CG​(x)|​(∑y∈CG​(x)p′χ⁡(y))=1|CG​(x)|p​⟨ResOp′​(CG​(x))G​(χ),1⟩.\frac{1}{|C_{G}(x)|}\left(\sum_{y\in C_{G}(x)_{p^{\prime}}}\chi(y)\right)=\frac{1}{|C_{G}(x)|_{p}}\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x))}(\chi),1\rangle.

Now let xx be a non-identity pp-element of GG. By Brauer’s Second Main Theorem, χ⁡(x)\chi(x) can be evaluated by considering only the irreducible constituents of ResCG​(x)G​(χ){\rm Res}^{G}_{C_{G}(x)}(\chi) which lie in the principal pp-block, and hence, in particular, have Op′​(CG​(x))O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x)) in their kernel. This certainly yields |χ⁡(x)|≤⟨ResOp′​(CG​(x))G​(χ),1⟩,|\chi(x)|\leq\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x))}(\chi),1\rangle, since χ⁡(x)\chi(x) is a sum of ⟨ResOp′​(CG​(x))G​(χ),1⟩\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x))}(\chi),1\rangle roots of unity. More precisely, we may conclude that (for each pp-element xx),

⟨ResOp′​(CG​(x))G​(χ),1⟩−χ⁡(x)\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x))}(\chi),1\rangle-\chi(x)

is a complex number with non-negative real part.

Now we have

⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩=∑1≠x∈Gp/G1|CG​(x)|p​(⟨ResOp′​(CG​(x))G​(χ),1⟩−χ⁡(x)).\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle=\sum_{1\neq x\in G_{p}/G}\frac{1}{|C_{G}(x)|_{p}}\left(\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x))}(\chi),1\rangle-\chi(x)\right).

This is a rational integer with non-negative real part, so is a non-negative integer. Hence we do have ⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩≥0,\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle\geq 0, and Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character, as χ\chi was an arbitrary non-trivial irreducible character in the principal pp-block.

Notice that in fact ⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle is strictly positive for χ\chi as above unless

χ⁡(g)=⟨ResOp′​(CG​(gp))G​(χ),1⟩\chi(g)=\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(g_{p}))}(\chi),1\rangle

for all pp-singular g∈G.g\in G. In particular, ⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle is strictly positive unless χ\chi takes non-negative rational integer values at all non-identity pp-elements of GG. Since χ\chi does not vanish on all non-identity pp-elements of GG, we may also note that if ⟨Ψ1,p,G,χ⟩=0,\langle\Psi_{1,p,G},\chi\rangle=0, then there is at least one non-identity pp-element xx such that χ⁡(x)\chi(x) takes a constant strictly positive rational integer value on the pp-section of xx, and, in particular, we must have ⟨ResOp′​(CG​(x))G​(χ),1⟩>0\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{p^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x))}(\chi),1\rangle>0 for this xx.

Corollary 7.4: Suppose that G≅PSL⁡(2,q)G\cong{\rm PSL}(2,q). Then the generalized character Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character of GG for each prime divisor pp of |G||G|.

Proof: There are three possible structures for the Sylow pp-subgroup PP of GG, and we note that in each of these cases, the centralizer of each non-identity pp-element of GG has a normal pp-complement. If PP is cyclic, then CG​(x)C_{G}(x) has a normal pp-complement for each non-identity element x∈P.x\in P. If p=2p=2 and PP is dihedral (allowing a Klein 4-group), then CG​(x)C_{G}(x) has a normal pp-complement for each non-identity element x∈Px\in P. If p|qp|q and PP is non-cyclic elementary Abelian, then CG​(x)C_{G}(x) is a pp-group for each non-identity element x∈P.x\in P.

8 Variants for sets of primes

Let π\pi be a set of prime divisors of the order of the finite group GG, and let n=|G|π,n=|G|_{\pi}, that is to say, the largest divisor of |G||G| which is only divisible by primes in π\pi. We may refer to nn as a Hall divisor of |G||G|.

Let Ψ1,π,G\Psi_{1,\pi,G} denote the class function of GG which takes value 00 on all π\pi-singular elements of GG and which takes the value ( the number of π\pi-elements of CG​(x)C_{G}(x)) on all π\pi-regular elements of GG.

Then Ψ1,π,G\Psi_{1,\pi,G} is a generalized character of GG, and Ψ1,π,G​(x)\Psi_{1,\pi,G}(x) is the number of nn-th roots of xx in GG, where n=|G|π.n=|G|_{\pi}. Furthermore, Ψ1,π,G\Psi_{1,\pi,G} is a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-linear combination of characters each induced from linear characters of Brauer elementary π′\pi^{\prime}-subgroups of GG, all proved in manner entirely analogous to the case π={p}.\pi=\{p\}.

It is also the case that if we let Gπ′/GG_{\pi^{\prime}}/G denote a full set of representatives for the conjugacy classes of π\pi-regular elements of GG, then we have

∑y∈Gπ′/GIndCG​(y)G​(Ψ1,π,CG​(y))=Λc,π,G\sum_{y\in G_{\pi^{\prime}}/G}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(y)}^{G}(\Psi_{1,\pi,C_{G}(y)})=\Lambda_{c,\pi,G}

where Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G} is the generalized character of GG which takes value |CG​(x)||C_{G}(x)| on π\pi-regular elements xx, and 00 on all π\pi-singular elements.

There is some computational evidence that Ψ1,π,G\Psi_{1,\pi,G} is always a character, but this remains unproven at present. We are thus interested in determining whether or not Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G} is a character, for if there is a group GG such that Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G} is not a character of GG, then there is a π\pi-regular element y∈Gy\in G such that Ψ1,π,CG​(y)\Psi_{1,\pi,C_{G}(y)} is not a character of CG​(y).C_{G}(y).

We recall that a π\pi-separable finite group GG is a finite group whose composition factors are all either π\pi-groups or π′\pi^{\prime}-groups. Every solvable group is π\pi-separable for every set of primes π.\pi.

Theorem 8.1: If GG is a π\pi-separable group, then Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G} is a character of GG, and Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G} is induced from a character of a Hall π′\pi^{\prime}-subgroup of GG.

Proof: Since GG is π\pi-separable, GG has a Hall π′\pi^{\prime}-subgroup HH. By the extension of Fong’s theory for pp-solvable groups in [7] to sets of primes for π\pi-separable groups by I.M. Isaacs in [9], we know that if GG has ℓ\ell conjugacy classes of π\pi-regular elements of GG, then there are ℓ\ell irreducible characters {ϕi:1≤i≤ℓ}\{\phi_{i}:1\leq i\leq\ell\} of G/Oπ​(G)G/O_{\pi}(G) (which we inflate to irreducible characters of GG), such that for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG, the restriction χ0\chi_{0} of χ\chi to Gπ′G_{\pi^{\prime}} is a non-negative integer combination of {ϕi,0:1≤i≤ℓ}\{\phi_{i,0}:1\leq i\leq\ell\}, and there are ℓ\ell distinct irreducible characters of HH, {αi:1≤i≤ℓ}\{\alpha_{i}:1\leq i\leq\ell\} such that

⟨ResHG​(ϕi),αj⟩=δi​j.\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{H}(\phi_{i}),\alpha_{j}\rangle=\delta_{ij}.

In particular, this implies that {ϕi:1≤i≤ℓ}\{\phi_{i}:1\leq i\leq\ell\} is linearly independent over ℂ.\mathbb{C}.

For each ii, if we let θj\theta_{j} denote the induced character IndHG​(αj),{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\alpha_{j}), then we have ⟨θj,αi⟩=δi,j.\langle\theta_{j},\alpha_{i}\rangle=\delta_{i,j}. Notice then that {θj:1≤j≤ℓ}\{\theta_{j}:1\leq j\leq\ell\} is linearly independent over ℂ\mathbb{C}, and forms a ℂ\mathbb{C}-basis for the space of complex-valued class functions of GG which vanish on all π\pi-singular elements of GG.

For if Λ\Lambda is any class function of GG which vanishes on all π\pi-singular elements of GG, then we have

Λ=∑i=1ℓ⟨Λ,ϕi⟩​θi.\Lambda=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\langle\Lambda,\phi_{i}\rangle\theta_{i}.

In particular, Λ\Lambda is a generalized character if and only if ⟨Λ,ϕi⟩∈ℤ\langle\Lambda,\phi_{i}\rangle\in\mathbb{Z} for each ii, and Λ\Lambda is a character if and only if ⟨Λ,ϕi⟩∈ℕ∪{0}\langle\Lambda,\phi_{i}\rangle\in\mathbb{N}\cup\{0\} for each ii. Notice, in particular, that Λ\Lambda is a character if and only if Λ\Lambda is induced from a character of HH.

So far, all is analogous to Fong’s theory for pp-solvable groups, and is as developed by I.M. Isaacs for π\pi-separable groups.

Here, the ϕi\phi_{i} are analogous to the Brauer characters in the usual modular theory. Now let yy be a π\pi-regular element of GG, and let χy\chi_{y} denote the characteristic function of the conjugacy class of yy. Then |CG​(y)|​χy|C_{G}(y)|\chi_{y} is a ℂ\mathbb{C}-linear combination of irreducible characters of GG, and certainly vanishes on π\pi-singular elements of GG, and we see easily using inner products as above that

|CG​(y)|​χy=∑i=1ℓϕi​(y−1)​θi.|C_{G}(y)|\chi_{y}=\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\phi_{i}(y^{-1})\theta_{i}.

Since each θi\theta_{i} vanishes on π\pi-singular elements, we conclude that the truncated conjugation class function Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G} coincides with the character

∑i=1ℓϕ¯i​θi,\sum_{i=1}^{\ell}\overline{\phi}_{i}\theta_{i},

and is induced from a character of HH (in fact from a non-negative integer combination of {αi:1≤i≤ℓ}\{\alpha_{i}:1\leq i\leq\ell\}), and this linear combination of the αi\alpha_{i} is unique subject to inducing to Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G}).

Now let us note that the coefficient of θi\theta_{i} in Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G} is ⟨Λc,π,G,ϕi⟩,\langle\Lambda_{c,\pi,G},\phi_{i}\rangle, and this is clearly ∑j=1ℓϕi​(yj)\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\phi_{i}(y_{j}), where {yj:1≤j≤ℓ}\{y_{j}:1\leq j\leq\ell\} is a set of representatives for the conjugacy classes of π\pi-regular elements of GG (for convenience, we choose these to be closed under inversion). Note, in particular, that this sum is always a non-negative integer (cf. a theorem of L.Solomon (in [16]) about complex irreducible characters).

Remark 8.2: C. Schroeder has informed us that he has independently obtained in unpublished work a different proof that the generalized character we call Λc,π,G\Lambda_{c,\pi,G} is a character when GG is π\pi-separable.

This seems an opportune moment to note that R. Boltje’s theory of Explicit Brauer Induction (see [1]) (which is a form of Brauer’s Induction Theorem commuting with restriction of characters) may be relevant to the question of whether Ψ1,π,G\Psi_{1,\pi,G} is a character of GG in general.

Boltje’s explicit Brauer induction theorem is compatible with Adams operations in a remarkable fashion. It guarantees that for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG, we may write

χ=∑(H,λ)/GaH,λ,χ​IndHG​(λ)\chi=\sum_{(H,\lambda)/G}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\lambda)

with each aH,λ,χ∈ℤ,a_{H,\lambda,\chi}\in\mathbb{Z}, each λ\lambda a linear character of the subgroup HH of GG, and furthermore, we also have (for every integer nn),

χ(n)=∑(H,λ)/GaH,λ,χ​IndHG​(λn),\chi^{(n)}=\sum_{(H,\lambda)/G}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\lambda^{n}),

where χ(n)​(g)=χ⁡(gn)\chi^{(n)}(g)=\chi(g^{n}) for all g∈Gg\in G.

Let us reconsider Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} in this light. In Section 1, we saw that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character of GG if and only if ⟨χ(q),1⟩≥0\langle\chi^{(q)},1\rangle\geq 0 for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG, where qq is a power of pp with q≥|G|pq\geq|G|_{p} and q≡1q\equiv 1 (mod |G|p′|G|_{p^{\prime}}).

If we write, as above,

χ=∑(H,λ)/GaH,λ,χ​IndHG​(λ)\chi=\sum_{(H,\lambda)/G}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\lambda)

such that we also have

χ(q)=∑(H,λ)/GaH,λ,χ​IndHG​(λq),\chi^{(q)}=\sum_{(H,\lambda)/G}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\lambda^{q}),

then we see easily that

⟨χ(q),1⟩=∑(H,λ):λq=1aH,λ,χ.\langle\chi^{(q)},1\rangle=\sum_{(H,\lambda):\lambda^{q}=1}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}.

Using similar arguments for π\pi we may deduce:

Theorem 8.3: i) Let GG be a finite group. Let pp be a prime divisor of |G||G| and let SS be a Sylow pp-subgroup of GG. Write (for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG, as we may)

χ=∑(H,λ)/GaH,λ,χ​IndHG​(λ),\chi=\sum_{(H,\lambda)/G}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\lambda),

where each aH,λ,χ∈ℤa_{H,\lambda,\chi}\in\mathbb{Z} and (H,λ)(H,\lambda) ranges over GG-conjugacy classes of pairs such that HH is a subgroup of GG and λ\lambda is a linear character of HH, where we also have (for every integer nn),

χ(n)=∑(H,λ)/GaH,λ,χ​IndHG​(λn),\chi^{(n)}=\sum_{(H,\lambda)/G}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\lambda^{n}),

where χ(n)​(g)=χ⁡(gn)\chi^{(n)}(g)=\chi(g^{n}) for each g∈G.g\in G. Then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character of GG if and only if

∑(H,λ,χ):λ|S|=1aH,λ,χ≥0\sum_{(H,\lambda,\chi):\lambda^{|S|}=1}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}\geq 0

for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG.

ii) Let GG be a finite group. Let π\pi be a set of primes and let mm be the π\pi-part of |G||G|. Write (for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG, as we may)

χ=∑(H,λ)/GaH,λ,χ​IndHG​(λ),\chi=\sum_{(H,\lambda)/G}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\lambda),

where each aH,λ,χ∈ℤa_{H,\lambda,\chi}\in\mathbb{Z} and (H,λ)(H,\lambda) ranges over GG-conjugacy classes of pairs such that HH is a subgroup of GG and λ\lambda is a linear character of HH, where we also have

χ(n)=∑(H,λ)/GaH,λ,χ​IndHG​(λn),\chi^{(n)}=\sum_{(H,\lambda)/G}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\lambda^{n}),

where χ(n)​(g)=χ⁡(gn)\chi^{(n)}(g)=\chi(g^{n}) for each g∈G.g\in G. Then Ψ1,π,G\Psi_{1,\pi,G} is a character of GG if and only if

∑(H,λ):λm=1aH,λ,χ≥0\sum_{(H,\lambda):\lambda^{m}=1}a_{H,\lambda,\chi}\geq 0

for each irreducible character χ\chi of GG.

9 The prime to the first power case, and groups with a strongly pp-embedded subgroup

Let GG be a finite group with Sylow pp-subgroup PP of order pp for pp a fixed prime. Let H=NG​(P)H=N_{G}(P) and let TT be a Hall p′p^{\prime}-subgroup of HH. Then from Theorem 3.2, we know that Ψ1,p,H\Psi_{1,p,H} is the character afforded by the projective cover of the trivial module, which is IndTH​(1){\rm Ind}_{T}^{H}(1).

We also know that

Ψ1,p,H=χr,H+∑1≠x∈P/HIndCH​(x)H​(χr,CH​(x)),\Psi_{1,p,H}=\chi_{r,H}+\sum_{1\neq x\in P/H}{\rm Ind}_{C_{H}(x)}^{H}(\chi_{r,C_{H}(x)}),

where χr,H\chi_{r,H} is the characteristic function of the set of pp-regular elements of H,H, etc.

Note that HH controls the conjugacy of elements of PP in GG, and notice also that

IndHG​(χr,H)−χr,G=IndHG​(1)−1.{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\chi_{r,H})-\chi_{r,G}={\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1)-1.

Now we have

Ψ1,p,G=χr,G+∑1≠x∈P/GIndCG​(x)G​(χr,CG​(x)).\Psi_{1,p,G}=\chi_{r,G}+\sum_{1\neq x\in P/G}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(x)}^{G}(\chi_{r,C_{G}(x)}).

Now we see that

IndHG​(Ψ1,p,H)−Ψ1,p,G=IndHG​(1)−1.{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,H})-\Psi_{1,p,G}={\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1)-1.

Hence we have

Ψ1,p,G=IndHG​(Ψ1,p,H)−IndHG​(1)+1.\Psi_{1,p,G}={\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,H})-{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1)+1.

Since we know that

Ψ1,p,H=IndTH​(1),\Psi_{1,p,H}={\rm Ind}_{T}^{H}(1),

we have now proved that in this case, we have:

Theorem 9.1: If the group GG has a Sylow pp-subgroup PP of order pp, then we have

Ψ1,p,G=1+IndTG​(1)−IndHG​(1),\Psi_{1,p,G}=1+{\rm Ind}_{T}^{G}(1)-{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1),

where H=NG​(P)H=N_{G}(P) and TT is a Hall p′p^{\prime}-subgroup of HH.

Remark 9.2: We note that in Theorem 9.1, the irreducible constituents of Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} are among the irreducible constituents of IndTG​(1).{\rm Ind}_{T}^{G}(1).

We claim next that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the character afforded by some projective R​GRG module. To see this, it suffices to prove that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} agrees on pp-regular elements with the Brauer character of a projective 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-module.

Let P1P_{1} denote the projective cover of the trivial 𝔽​H\mathbb{F}H-module 𝔽,\mathbb{F}, whose Brauer character agrees with Ψ1,p,H\Psi_{1,p,H} on pp-regular elements. Let us write

IndHG​(𝔽)=𝔽⊕Q,{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\mathbb{F})=\mathbb{F}\oplus Q,

where QQ is projective. We need to prove that IndHG​(P1){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(P_{1}) has an indecomposable summand isomorphic to QQ. Since projective 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-modules are injective, it suffices to prove that IndHG​(P1){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(P_{1}) has a submodule isomorphic to Q.Q. But IndHG​(𝔽){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\mathbb{F}) is certainly isomorphic to a submodule of IndHG​(P1),{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(P_{1}), so this is clear.

Theorem 9.3: Suppose that GG is a finite group which has a (proper) strongly pp-embedded subgroup HH. Suppose further that Ψ1,p,H\Psi_{1,p,H} may be afforded by a projective R​HRH-module MM. Then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

Proof: We mimic the proof in the case that the Sylow pp-subgroup of GG had order pp. Just as in the preamble to 9.1, we see

IndHG​(Ψ1,p,H)−Ψ1,p,G=IndHG​(1)−1,{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,H})-\Psi_{1,p,G}={\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1)-1,

so that

Ψ1,p,G=1+IndHG​(Ψ1,p,H)−IndHG​(1).\Psi_{1,p,G}=1+{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,H})-{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1).

Since Ψ1,p,H\Psi_{1,p,H} is assumed to be a character, and contains the trivial character with multiplicity one, it is clear that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character (still containing the trivial character with multiplicity one).

Now let MM be a projective 𝔽​H\mathbb{F}H-module whose Brauer character agrees with Ψ1,p,H\Psi_{1,p,H} on pp-regular elements of HH. Since HH is strongly pp-embedded in GG, we may write

IndHG​(𝔽)=𝔽⊕Q,{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\mathbb{F})=\mathbb{F}\oplus Q,

where QQ is a projective 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-module.

It suffices to prove that, in the Green ring of 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-modules,

𝔽+IndHG​(M)−IndHG​(𝔽)\mathbb{F}+{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(M)-{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\mathbb{F})

represents a genuine projective 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-module. For this, it is enough to show that IndHG​(M){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(M) has a direct summand isomorphic to QQ. Now MM has a direct summand which is the projective cover of the trivial 𝔽​H\mathbb{F}H-module. Hence the socle of MM has a trivial summand and IndHG​(𝔽){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(\mathbb{F}) is certainly isomorphic to a submodule of IndHG​(M){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(M). In particular, QQ is isomorphic to a direct summand of IndHG​(M){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(M) (since QQ is projective, and hence also injective), as required.

Remark 9.4: In fact, MM has at least two trivial composition factors since the projective cover of the trivial 𝔽​H\mathbb{F}H-module has trivial head and trivial socle, so that QQ occurs with multiplicity at least two as a summand of IndHG​(M){\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(M), and the lift of QQ to a projective R​GRG-module occurs as a direct summand of the projective R​GRG-module affording Ψ1,p,G.\Psi_{1,p,G}. Furthermore, it is easy to check that the projective cover of the trivial 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-module is not isomorphic to a direct summand of QQ.

Theorem 9.5: If GG has a cyclic Sylow pp-subgroup SS, then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

Proof: We proceed by induction on |S||S|, the result being clear when |S|=1,|S|=1, so suppose that |S|>1|S|>1 and the result is true for groups GG with a Sylow pp-subgroup of order less than |S||S|. If Op​(G)≠1,O_{p}(G)\neq 1, then by induction Ψ1,p,G/Op​(G)\Psi_{1,p,G/O_{p}(G)} is afforded by a projective R​G/Op​(G)RG/O_{p}(G)-module XX, and then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is afforded by the projective cover of (the inflation of) XX as R​GRG-module. Hence we may suppose that Op​(G)=1.O_{p}(G)=1.

But then N=NG​(Ω1​(P))N=N_{G}(\Omega_{1}(P)) is a proper strongly pp-embedded subgroup of GG, where Ω1​(P)\Omega_{1}(P) is the unique subgroup of PP of order pp, and furthermore, Ψ1,p,N\Psi_{1,p,N} is afforded by a projective R​NRN-module by the argument of the previous paragraph. By Theorem 9.3, Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

We also mention another case of interest, which is a special case of Theorem 9.3, after noting that

Ψ1,p,H=IndTH​(1)\Psi_{1,p,H}={\rm Ind}_{T}^{H}(1)

by part iii) of Theorem 3.2.

Corollary 9.6: Suppose that GG has a T​ITI-Sylow pp-subgroup PP. Let H=NG​(P)H=N_{G}(P) and TT be a Hall p′p^{\prime}-subgroup of HH. Then

Ψ1,p,G=1+IndTG​(1)−IndHG​(1)\Psi_{1,p,G}=1+{\rm Ind}_{T}^{G}(1)-{\rm Ind}_{H}^{G}(1)

is a character which may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

10 More on the Truncated Conjugation Module

We recall that the Tc,p,G,T_{c,p,G}, the truncated conjugation module, is the projective R​GRG-module whose character takes value 00 on each pp-singular element of GG, and value |CG​(x)||C_{G}(x)| on each pp-regular element of GG. We propose the following:

Conjecture A: For each p′p^{\prime}-element xx of GG, the RR-valued class function Ψx,p,G\Psi_{x,p,G} which agrees on pp-regular elements with the character afforded by the conjugation action on the p′p^{\prime}-section of xx in GG, and which vanishes on all pp-singular elements, is a character, and may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module Px,p,GP_{x,p,G}. Consequently,

Tc,p,G=⨁x∈Gp′/GPx,p,G.T_{c,p,G}=\bigoplus_{x\in G_{p^{\prime}/G}}P_{x,p,G}.

Lemma 10.1: To prove Conjecture A, it suffices to treat (for all GG) the case that x=1G.x=1_{G}.

Proof: Suppose that for every finite group HH, we know that the class function Ψ1,p,H\Psi_{1,p,H} which agrees with the permutation character

∑y∈Hp/HIndCH​(y)H​(1)\sum_{y\in H_{p}/H}{\rm Ind}_{C_{H}(y)}^{H}(1)

on pp-regular elements, and vanishes elsewhere, is a character, and is afforded by a projective R​HRH-module. We claim that Conjecture A holds for GG.

Suppose first that GG contains a non-trivial central pp-regular element z.z. Then, as noted at the end of Remark 5.1,

Ψz,p,G=Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{z,p,G}=\Psi_{1,p,G}

and Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the inflation to GG of

Ψ1,p,G/⟨z⟩.\Psi_{1,p,G/\langle z\rangle}.

By hypothesis, Ψ1,p,G/⟨z⟩\Psi_{1,p,G/\langle z\rangle} is afforded by a projective R​G/⟨z⟩RG/\langle z\rangle-module, which may be regarded as (ie inflates to) a projective R​GRG-module.

Now let xx be any non-central pp-regular element of GG. Then Conjecture A holds for CG​(x).C_{G}(x). The class function Ψx,p,G\Psi_{x,p,G} is clearly induced from Ψx,p,CG​(x).\Psi_{x,p,C_{G}(x)}. This last class function is afforded by the projective R​CG​(x)RC_{G}(x)-module Px,p,CG​(x),P_{x,p,C_{G}(x)}, arguing as in the paragraph above. Hence Ψx,p,G\Psi_{x,p,G} is a character and is afforded by the projective R​GRG-module IndCG​(x)G​(Px,p,CG​(x)).{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(x)}^{G}(P_{x,p,C_{G}(x)}). Thus Conjecture A holds for G.G.

Hence proving Conjecture A has been reduced to proving:

Conjecture B: The class function Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} which takes value (the number of pp-elements of CG​(x)C_{G}(x)) on each pp-regular x∈G,x\in G, and which vanishes on all pp-singular elements of G,G, is a character of GG which may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

Corollary 10.2: Conjecture B holds for G=PSL⁡(2,q)G={\rm PSL}(2,q) for every odd prime pp, and also holds for p=2p=2 if qq is even.

Proof: Let H=NG​(P),H=N_{G}(P), where PP is a Sylow pp-subgroup of GG. If pp is odd, then either PP is cyclic, or else qq is a power of pp and PP is elementary Abelian. If qq is even and p=2,p=2, then PP is elementary Abelian, and HH is strongly (2)-embedded. By Theorem 3.2, Ψ1,p,H\Psi_{1,p,H} is a character afforded by a projective R​HRH-module in all cases. Hence the result follows by Theorem 9.3 and Theorem 9.5.

Remark 10.3: It is true that Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} is a character whenever G=PSL⁡(2,q)G={\rm PSL}(2,q), and that the contribution to Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} from non-principal 22-blocks is afforded by a projective module, as noted in 7.1 and 7.3.

We note here the following alternative direct proof that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a generalized character.

Lemma 10.4: The class function Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a generalized character, and is afforded by a ℤ\mathbb{Z}-linear combination of projective R​GRG-modules (in the Green ring for R​GRG).

Proof: We know that Λc,p,G\Lambda_{c,p,G} is the character afforded by the projective R​GRG-module Tc,p,G.T_{c,p,G}. We also know that

Λc,p,G=∑y∈Gp′/GIndCG​(y)G​(Ψ1,p,CG​(y)/⟨y⟩),\Lambda_{c,p,G}=\sum_{y\in G_{p^{\prime}}/G}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(y)}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,C_{G}(y)/\langle y\rangle}),

so the result follows by induction (by assuming that the result is true for groups of order less than |G||G|, we may suppose that Ψ1,p,CG​(y)/⟨y⟩\Psi_{1,p,C_{G}(y)/\langle y\rangle} is a generalized character whenever 1≠y∈Gp′1\neq y\in G_{p^{\prime}} (afforded by a virtual projective). We also know that Λc,p,G\Lambda_{c,p,G} is a character which may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module).

11 Local control of the permutation action on non-identity pp-elements

Let 𝒮p​(G)\mathcal{S}_{p}(G) denote the simplicial complex associated to the poset of non-trivial pp-subgroups of GG. As usual, when σ\sigma is an element of 𝒮p​(G)\mathcal{S}_{p}(G), we denote the number of non-trivial pp-subgroups in σ\sigma by |σ|.|\sigma|.

The first result of this section illustrates that the conjugation action of GG on its non-identity pp-elements is pp-locally controlled in a precise sense. This is relevant to the study of Ψ1,p,G,\Psi_{1,p,G}, because Ψ1,p,G−1\Psi_{1,p,G}-1 agrees on pp-regular elements with the character afforded by the conjugation action of GG on its non-identity pp-elements.

Theorem 11.1: Let GG be a finite group, and RR be as before. For HH a subgroup of GG, let Xp,HX_{p,H} denote the permutation module of HH afforded by the conjugation action on its non-identity pp-elements. Then in the Green ring of R​GRG, we have

∑σ∈𝒮p​(G)/G(−1)|σ|​IndGσG​(Xp,Gσ)=0.\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_{p}(G)/G}(-1)^{|\sigma|}{\rm Ind}_{G_{\sigma}}^{G}(X_{p,G_{\sigma}})=0.

In particular, the virtual character

∑σ∈𝒮p​(G)/G(−1)|σ|​IndGσG​(Ψ1,p,Gσ−1)\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_{p}(G)/G}(-1)^{|\sigma|}{\rm Ind}_{G_{\sigma}}^{G}(\Psi_{1,p,G_{\sigma}}-1)

vanishes on all pp-regular elements of GG.

Proof: We work instead with the simplicial complex 𝒮p+​(G)\mathcal{S}^{+}_{p}(G) associated to the poset of ordered pairs (Q,x)(Q,x) whose 11-simplices are ordered pairs (Q,x)(Q,x) with QQ a non-trivial pp-subgroup of GG and xx a non-identity pp-element of GG normalizing QQ. We decree that (Q,x)≤(P,y)(Q,x)\leq(P,y) if and only if x=yx=y and Q≤P.Q\leq P.

Then it is clear that the alternating sum of permutation modules in the statement of the Theorem is equal to

∑τ∈𝒮p+​(G)/G(−1)|τ|​IndGτG​(R)\sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{S}^{+}_{p}(G)/G}(-1)^{|\tau|}{\rm Ind}_{G_{\tau}}^{G}(R)

in the Green ring for R​GRG, where we include the empty chain, and consider it to have stabilizer GG and length zero. Notice that the empty chain of 𝒮p​(G)\mathcal{S}_{p}(G) contributes

∑1≠x∈Gp/GIndCG​(x)G​(R)\sum_{1\neq x\in G_{p}/G}{\rm Ind}_{C_{G}(x)}^{G}(R)

to the original alternating sum of modules, and that this is cancelled by the contribution from the length one chains in {(⟨x⟩,x):1≠x∈Gp/G}.\{(\langle x\rangle,x):1\neq x\in G_{p}/G\}.

For the proof, we employ a familiar cancellation argument. For a given pp-element x∈G#,x\in G^{\#}, we may reduce the contribution from chains of elements with second component xx to that from those chains of elements (Q,x)(Q,x) with [Q,x]=1.[Q,x]=1. If

τ=(Q1,x)<(Q2,x)<…​(Qn,x)\tau=(Q_{1},x)<(Q_{2},x)<\ldots(Q_{n},x)

is a chain not of this form, choose rr minimal such that [Qr,x]≠1[Q_{r},x]\neq 1 (possibly r=1r=1) and form a chain τ∗\tau^{\ast} by inserting CQr​(x)C_{Q_{r}}(x) between Qr−1Q_{r-1} and QrQ_{r} (or at the beginning if r=1r=1) in case Qr−1≠CQr​(x)Q_{r-1}\neq C_{Q_{r}}(x), while if Qr−1=CQr​(x),Q_{r-1}=C_{Q_{r}}(x), we form τ∗\tau^{\ast} by deleting Qr−1Q_{r-1} from τ.\tau. Then it is easy to check that τ∗⁣∗=τ,\tau^{\ast\ast}=\tau, and that Gτ∗=Gτ,G_{\tau^{\ast}}=G_{\tau}, so that the contributions from τ\tau and τ∗\tau^{\ast} cancel.

Hence we now only need to consider (all) chains of elements (Q,x)∈𝒮p+​(G)(Q,x)\in\mathcal{S}^{+}_{p}(G) such that [Q,x]=1.[Q,x]=1. For each non-identity pp-element x,x, we may delete the contribution from remaining chains with second component xx by a similar pairing argument to that above, using respectively the monotonic maps

(Q,x)→(Q​⟨x⟩,x)(Q,x)\to(Q\langle x\rangle,x)

and

(Q​⟨x⟩,x)→(⟨x⟩,x).(Q\langle x\rangle,x)\to(\langle x\rangle,x).

To expand: if we take a representative xx for a class of non-identity pp-elements of GG, and we consider a chain

τ=(Q1,x)<(Q2,x)<…<(Qn,x)\tau=(Q_{1},x)<(Q_{2},x)<\ldots<(Q_{n},x)

where each QiQ_{i} is a subgroup of CG​(x)C_{G}(x) containing xx, then we may cancel the contribution to our alternating sum from the chain τ\tau whenever Q1>⟨x⟩Q_{1}>\langle x\rangle using the chain

(⟨x⟩,x)<(Q1,x)<…<(Qn,x)(\langle x\rangle,x)<(Q_{1},x)<\ldots<(Q_{n},x)

in the case that Q1Q_{1} strictly contains xx , while if Q1=⟨x⟩Q_{1}=\langle x\rangle and n>1n>1 we cancel using the chain

(Q2,x)<…<(Qn,x).(Q_{2},x)<\ldots<(Q_{n},x).

If Q1=⟨x⟩Q_{1}=\langle x\rangle and n=1n=1 then we cancel the contribution from the singleton chain (⟨x⟩,x)(\langle x\rangle,x) using the pair (1,x)(1,x) as discussed at the beginning of the proof.

Before our next result, we recall that

∑σ∈𝒮p​(G)/G(−1)|σ|​IndGσG​(R)=Stp​(G),\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_{p}(G)/G}(-1)^{|\sigma|}{\rm Ind}_{G_{\sigma}}^{G}(R)={\rm St}_{p}(G),

is the Steinberg (virtual) module for GG, as defined (up to sign convention) by P.J.Webb (see, e.g. [17]). This was proved by Webb to be a virtually projective R​GRG-module.

Corollary 11.2 : Let P1,p,GP_{1,p,G} denote the (unique) virtual projective module in the Green ring of R​GRG affording the virtual character Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G}. Then we have

∑σ∈𝒮p​(G)/G(−1)|σ|​IndGσG​(P1,p,Gσ−R)=0\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_{p}(G)/G}(-1)^{|\sigma|}{\rm Ind}_{G_{\sigma}}^{G}(P_{1,p,G_{\sigma}}-R)=0

in the Green ring for R​GRG. In particular,

∑σ∈𝒮p​(G)/G(−1)|σ|​IndGσG​(P1,p,Gσ)=Stp​(G).\sum_{\sigma\in\mathcal{S}_{p}(G)/G}(-1)^{|\sigma|}{\rm Ind}_{G_{\sigma}}^{G}(P_{1,p,G_{\sigma}})={\rm St}_{p}(G).

Proof: The virtual module in the statement of the Corollary is a virtual projective R​GRG-module, as each P1,p,GσP_{1,p,G_{\sigma}} is a virtual projective. Hence to prove that it is the zero module, it is sufficient (by the non-singularity of the Cartan matrix) to prove that the alternating sum given affords the zero character. However, since it is a virtual projective, its virtual character vanishes on all pp-singular elements. Also, as noted in Theorem 11.1, its virtual character vanishes on all pp-regular elements, so the proof of the Corollary is complete.

Theorem 11.3: In the Green ring for R​GRG, the virtual projective module P1,p,GP_{1,p,G} is equal to

∑Q/GIndNG​(Q)G(P[Stp(NG(Q)/Q))]),\sum_{Q/G}{\rm Ind}^{G}_{N_{G}(Q)}(P[{\rm St}_{p}\left(N_{G}(Q)/Q)\right)]),

where Q/GQ/G is a set of representatives for the GG-conjugacy classes of pp-subgroups of GG such that Q=Op​(NG​(Q)),Q=O_{p}(N_{G}(Q)), and where P⁡[M]P[M] indicates that we are taking the (well-defined) projective cover of a virtual projective R​NG​(Q)/QRN_{G}(Q)/Q-module MM as (virtual) R​NG​(Q)RN_{G}(Q)-module.

Proof: We work with the complex 𝒩p​(G),\mathcal{N}_{p}(G), where the simplices consist of chains of (strictly increasing) mutually normalizing pp-subgroups, which is interchangeable with 𝒮p​(G)\mathcal{S}_{p}(G) in all calculations needed here.

We first note that (in the Green ring for R​GRG), from Corollary 11.2, we may write

We now aim to prove that Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} is afforded by a projective R​GRG-module. By the results of Section 7, it suffices to prove that Ψ1,2,G(b)\Psi_{1,2,G}^{(b)} is afforded by a projective R​GRG-module, where bb is the principal block of R​GRG. We have
[NG(S):CG(S)]∈{1,3},[N_{G}(S):C_{G}(S)]\in\{1,3\}, where S∈Syl2​(G).S\in{\rm Syl}_{2}(G). If NG​(S)=CG​(S),N_{G}(S)=C_{G}(S), then GG has a normal 22-complement, and by Theorem 3.2, Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module. Suppose then that [NG(S):CG(S)]=3.[N_{G}(S):C_{G}(S)]=3.

In that case, GG has a single conjugacy class of involutions, say with representative tt. Furthermore, the principal 22-block bb of GG contains four irreducible characters, all of odd degree, and we have ℓ⁡(b)=3.\ell(b)=3. Let θ1\theta_{1} denote the character of the projective cover of the trivial module. Then θ1\theta_{1} is real-valued, and all its irreducible constituents lie in the block bb.

Let 1,χ2,χ3,χ41,\chi_{2},\chi_{3},\chi_{4} be the set of irreducible characters in bb. Then there are signs 1,ϵ2,ϵ3,ϵ41,\epsilon_{2},\epsilon_{3},\epsilon_{4} such that

β=1+ϵ2​χ2+ϵ3​χ3+ϵ4​χ4\beta=1+\epsilon_{2}\chi_{2}+\epsilon_{3}\chi_{3}+\epsilon_{4}\chi_{4}

vanishes on all 22-regular elements, and β\beta takes value 44 on all 22-singular elements (note that ϵi=χi​(t)\epsilon_{i}=\chi_{i}(t) for OPEN2≤i≤4).2\leq i\leq 4). Note also that t​xtx has no square root in GG whenever xx is an element of odd order in CG​(t),C_{G}(t), so that 1+∑i=24ϵi​ν​(χi)=0,1+\sum_{i=2}^{4}\epsilon_{i}\nu(\chi_{i})=0, by Brauer’s Second and Third Main Theorems.

Suppose first that χ2\chi_{2} is not real-valued. Then

∑g∈Gχ2​(g)=0.\sum_{g\in G}\chi_{2}(g)=0.

Also, we know that

∑g∈Gχ2​(g2)=0\sum_{g\in G}\chi_{2}(g^{2})=0

since χ2\chi_{2} has Frobenius-Schur indicator 00. This leads to

|G|4​(⟨ResO2′​(CG​(t))G​(χ2),1⟩)=ϵ2​|G|4,\frac{|G|}{4}\left(\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{2^{\prime}}(C_{G}(t))}(\chi_{2}),1\rangle\right)=\epsilon_{2}\frac{|G|}{4},

which forces ϵ2\epsilon_{2} to be non-negative, and hence ϵ2=1\epsilon_{2}=1. But in that case, we may also assume that χ3=χ2¯\chi_{3}=\overline{\chi_{2}} and so also ϵ3=1.\epsilon_{3}=1. This now forces ϵ4=−1\epsilon_{4}=-1 and ν⁡(χ4)=1.\nu(\chi_{4})=1.

In this case, then, we have Ψ1,2,G(b)=1+χ4.\Psi_{1,2,G}^{(b)}=1+\chi_{4}.

Now suppose that χi\chi_{i} is real-valued for 2≤i≤4.2\leq i\leq 4. Then χi\chi_{i} has Frobenius-Schur indicator 11 for 1≤i≤41\leq i\leq 4, and we have

Ψ1,2,G(b)=1+χ2+χ3+χ4.\Psi_{1,2,G}^{(b)}=1+\chi_{2}+\chi_{3}+\chi_{4}.

By results of Erdmann [5,6] and Landrock [10] (and earlier results of Brauer) we know that all decomposition numbers for bb are 00 or 11. Also, up to ordering of simple bb-modules, there are only two possibilities for the Cartan matrix of bb. These are

(422221212)\left(\begin{array}[]{clcr}4&2&2\\ 2&2&1\\ 2&1&2\end{array}\right)

and

(211121112).\left(\begin{array}[]{clcr}2&1&1\\ 1&2&1\\ 1&1&2\end{array}\right).

In the former case, where bb is Morita equivalent to the principal 22-block of A5,A_{5}, the character of the projective cover of the trivial module has norm-squared 4. In the second case where bb is Morita equivalent to the principal 22-block of A4,A_{4}, the character of the projective cover of the trivial module has norm squared 2.2.

In all cases, we may conclude that Ψ1,2,G(b)=θ1,\Psi_{1,2,G}^{(b)}=\theta_{1}, the character afforded by the projective cover of the trivial module. For if ⟨θ1,θ1⟩=4,\langle\theta_{1},\theta_{1}\rangle=4, and

Ψ1,2,G(b)=1+χ4,\Psi_{1,2,G}^{(b)}=1+\chi_{4},

then we are forced to conclude that χ2+χ3\chi_{2}+\chi_{3} vanishes on 22-singular elements when χ2\chi_{2} is not real valued. However, χ2\chi_{2} and χ3\chi_{3} agree and do not vanish on 22-singular elements in that case, a contradiction.

On the other hand, in the case that χ2,χ3,χ4\chi_{2},\chi_{3},\chi_{4} are all real-valued and

θ1=1+χ2,\theta_{1}=1+\chi_{2},

(without loss of generality), then we may label so that ϵ2=−1=ϵ4=−ϵ3,\epsilon_{2}=-1=\epsilon_{4}=-\epsilon_{3}, since 1+ϵ2+ϵ3+ϵ4=0.1+\epsilon_{2}+\epsilon_{3}+\epsilon_{4}=0. But the only characters of projective indecomposable R​GRG-modules in bb which are consistent with the Cartan matrix for bb in this case are 1+χ2,χ2+χ31+\chi_{2},\chi_{2}+\chi_{3} and χ2+χ4,\chi_{2}+\chi_{4}, and these do not all vanish at tt. Hence we have proved:

Theorem 13.1: Suppose that GG is a finite group whose Sylow 22-subgroup is a Klein 44-group. Then Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

In particular, we have:

Corollary 13.2: Suppose that G≅PSL⁡(2,q)G\cong{\rm PSL}(2,q) with q≢±1q\not\equiv\pm 1 (mod 88). Then Conjecture B holds for GG (for each prime divisor pp of |G||G|).

Proof: If q=2,q=2, then GG has a normal 22-complement and a normal Sylow 33-subgroup. If q=3,q=3, then GG has a normal 33-complement and a normal Sylow 22-subgroup. Theorem 3.2 may be applied in these cases.

If q>3,q>3, then GG is a finite simple group. Let pp be a prime divisor of |G||G|. If pp divides q,q, then GG has a characteristic pp type BN-pair and Ψ1,2,p\Psi_{1,2,p} is the square of the Steinberg character. Hence we may suppose that q>3q>3 and pp does not divide qq. If pp is odd, then GG has a cyclic Sylow pp-subgroup, so that Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character afforded by a projective R​GRG-module. If p=2,p=2, then GG has a Klein 44 Sylow 22-subgroup and the result follows by 13.1.

14 Conjecture BB for G=PSL⁡(2,q)G={\rm PSL}(2,q) when PSL⁡(2,q){\rm PSL}(2,q) has order divisible by 88

Throughout this section, we suppose that G≅PSL⁡(2,q)G\cong{\rm PSL}(2,q) with qq odd and that GG has a dihedral Sylow 22-subgroup with at least 88 elements. Notice that GG has one conjugacy class of involutions in this case, say with representative tt. Our aim is to prove that Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} is a character of GG which may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module. This will complete the proof that Conjecture B holds for GG for all primes when G≅PSL⁡(2,q)G\cong{\rm PSL}(2,q). By the results of Sections 7,9 and 13, it only remains to deal with the case p=2p=2 when GG has a dihedral Sylow 22-subgroup of order at least 88, and we need to prove that whenever ϕi\phi_{i} is an absolutely irreducible Brauer character in the principal 22-block of R​GRG, then

⟨Ψ1,2,G,ϕ⟩≥0.\langle\Psi_{1,2,G},\phi\rangle\geq 0.

There are two cases to consider:

Case 1: q≡1q\equiv 1 (mod 88). In this case, CG​(t)C_{G}(t) is a dihedral group with q−1q-1 elements, and has a unique cyclic subgroup HH of index 22. Write H=K×LH=K\times L where KK has odd order and LL is a 22-group. Then K=O2′​(CG​(x))K=O_{2^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x)) for each non-identity element x∈L.x\in L.

The character table of GG was known to Frobenius. Combining this with the results of Brauer, Erdmann and Landrock mentioned in the previous section, we have the following information: GG has exactly four irreducible characters of odd degree (respectively of degree 1,q,q+12,q+121,q,\frac{q+1}{2},\frac{q+1}{2}), and these all lie in the principal 22-block bb of GG (in general, as noted by R. Brauer, any 22-block of defect greater than one contains at least 44 irreducible characters of odd degree).

GG has q−14\frac{q-1}{4} irreducible characters of degree q−1q-1, which all lie in 22-blocks of defect zero of GG.

GG has q−54\frac{q-5}{4} irreducible characters of degree q+1q+1, and |L|2−1\frac{|L|}{2}-1 of these are (all) the height one irreducible characters in the principal 22-block of GG.

By the results of Section VII of (Burkhardt, [3]) we know in this case that the Brauer character (for the prime 22) of a (complex) irreducible character χ\chi of degree q+12\frac{q+1}{2} decomposes on reduction (mod J⁡(R)J(R) ) as 1+ϕ1+\phi where ϕ\phi is a Brauer irreducible character of degree q−12.\frac{q-1}{2}. We claim that

⟨Ψ1,2,G,ϕ⟩≥0.\langle\Psi_{1,2,G},\phi\rangle\geq 0.

By Theorem 7.3, we know that

⟨Ψ1,2,G,χ⟩≥0,\langle\Psi_{1,2,G},\chi\rangle\geq 0,

so we only need to exclude the possibility that ⟨Ψ1,2,G,χ⟩=0,\langle\Psi_{1,2,G},\chi\rangle=0, since we know that ⟨Ψ1,2,G,1⟩=1.\langle\Psi_{1,2,G},1\rangle=1.

The argument at the end of the proof of 7.3 shows that the only way we can obtain ⟨Ψ1,2,G,χ⟩=0\langle\Psi_{1,2,G},\chi\rangle=0 is if we have

⟨ResO2′​(CG​(x))G​(χ),1⟩=χ⁡(x)\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{2^{\prime}}(C_{G}(x))}(\chi),1\rangle=\chi(x)

for each non-identity 22-element x∈G.x\in G. But in this case, O2′​(CG​(t))O_{2^{\prime}}(C_{G}(t)) is cyclic of order at most q−18\frac{q-1}{8} for an involution t∈Gt\in G, and χ\chi takes constant value 11 on non-identity elements of O2′​(CG​(t))O_{2^{\prime}}(C_{G}(t)), (because the Borel subgroup BB of PSL⁡(2,q){\rm PSL}(2,q) is a Frobenius group of order q⁡(q−1)2\frac{q(q-1)}{2} and, (using unimodularity), ResBG​(χ){\rm Res}^{G}_{B}(\chi) decomposes as 1+μ,1+\mu, where μ\mu is irreducible of degree q−12\frac{q-1}{2} and μ\mu vanishes on all non-identity elements of the cyclic Frobenius complement). Hence

⟨ResO2′​(CG​(t))G​(χ),1⟩≥8​(q+1)2​(q−1)>4,\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{2^{\prime}}(C_{G}(t))}(\chi),1\rangle\geq\frac{8(q+1)}{2(q-1)}>4,

so we certainly have

⟨ResO2′​(CG​(t))G​(χ),1⟩>1=χ⁡(t)\langle{\rm Res}^{G}_{O_{2^{\prime}}(C_{G}(t))}(\chi),1\rangle>1=\chi(t)

and hence ⟨Ψ1,2,G,χ⟩≥1,\langle\Psi_{1,2,G},\chi\rangle\geq 1, as required to prove the claim.

Since it was known to Brauer that there are three absolutely irreducible Brauer characters in the principal 22-block of GG in this case, and from [3], we know that these are the trivial Brauer character and two algebraically conjugate irreducible Brauer characters of degree q−12,\frac{q-1}{2}, we may conclude in this case that Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} has non-negative inner product with each Brauer irreducible character of GG, so that Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

Case 2 : q≡−1q\equiv-1 (mod 88).

In this case, we know from [3] again that there are three absolutely irreducible Brauer characters in the principal 22-block of GG, and they again have respective degrees 1,q−12,q−12.1,\frac{q-1}{2},\frac{q-1}{2}. However, in this case, these are all obtained by reduction (mod J⁡(R)J(R)) of complex irreducible characters of GG (this time, the odd degree irreducible characters in the principal 22-block have respective degrees 1,q,q−12,q−121,q,\frac{q-1}{2},\frac{q-1}{2}). By Theorem 7.3, it follows that ⟨Ψ1,2,G,ϕ⟩≥0\langle\Psi_{1,2,G},\phi\rangle\geq 0 for each Brauer irreducible character ϕ\phi, so that we have completed the proof that Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

Theorem 14.1: Suppose that G≅PSL⁡(2,q)G\cong{\rm PSL}(2,q) where qq is a prime power. Then for each prime pp, the generalized character Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character which may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

In fact, using Theorem 3.2, we may deduce:

Corollary 14.2: Suppose that G≅SL⁡(2,q)G\cong{\rm SL}(2,q) where qq is a prime power. Then for each prime pp, the generalized character Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is a character which may be afforded by a projective R​GRG-module.

Proof: If pp is an odd prime divisor of |SL⁡(2,q)|,|{\rm SL}(2,q)|, then Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} contains the central involution of SL⁡(2,q){\rm SL}(2,q) in its kernel, and the result follows by 14.1. If p=2,p=2, then by Theorem 3.2 we may deduce that Ψ1,2,G\Psi_{1,2,G} is afforded by the projective cover of MM as R​GRG-module, where Ψ1,2,G/Z⁡(G)\Psi_{1,2,G/Z(G)} is afforded by the projective R​G/Z⁡(G)RG/Z(G)-module MM.

15 The truncated conjugation module as a direct summand of copies of the regular module

Theorem 15.1 : The truncated conjugation module Tc,p,GT_{c,p,G} is a direct summand of the direct sum of ℓ\ell copies of the regular R​GRG-module, and is not a direct summand of the direct sum of rr copies of the regular module for any r<ℓ.r<\ell.

Proof: We know that the projective cover of the trivial module occurs with multiplicity ℓ\ell as a summand of Tc,p,GT_{c,p,G}, while it only occurs with multiplicity one as a direct summand of the regular module R​GRG. Hence the second assertion is clear. To prove the first assertion, it suffices to pove that for 1≤i≤ℓ,1\leq i\leq\ell, the character θi\theta_{i} occurs with multiplicity at most ℓ​ϕi​(1)\ell\phi_{i}(1) as a summand of Λc,p,G\Lambda_{c,p,G}. But this multiplicity is ∑j=1ℓϕi​(yj)\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\phi_{i}(y_{j}), which is a non-negative integer less than or equal to ℓ​ϕi​(1).\ell\phi_{i}(1).

Corollary 15.2: Whenever P1,p,GP_{1,p,G} is a projective R​GRG-module, then it is a direct summand of the regular R​GRG-module.

Proof: It suffices to prove that for i≤ℓ,i\leq\ell, the multiplicity of θi\theta_{i} in Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is at most ϕi​(1).\phi_{i}(1). This multiplicity is

∑j=1ℓϕi​(yj)​|Gp∩CG​(yj)||CG​(yj)|.\sum_{j=1}^{\ell}\frac{\phi_{i}(y_{j})|G_{p}\cap C_{G}(y_{j})|}{|C_{G}(y_{j})|}.

Since the multiplicity of the character θ1\theta_{1} of the projective cover of the trivial module in Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is one, we see easily that the multiplicity of θi\theta_{i} is at most ϕi​(1)\phi_{i}(1), and that equality occurs if and only if Op​(G)≤ker​ϕi,O^{p}(G)\leq{\rm ker}\phi_{i}, in other words, equality can only occur when i=1i=1 and ϕi\phi_{i} is the trivial Brauer character. Hence we have proved that θi\theta_{i} occurs with multiplicity at most ϕi​(1)−1\phi_{i}(1)-1 in Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} for i>1.i>1.

Remark 15.3: In particular, whether or not P1,p,GP_{1,p,G} is a projective R​GRG-module, the only character afforded by the projective cover (as R​GRG-module) of a one-dimensional simple 𝔽​G\mathbb{F}G-module which occurs with non-zero multiplicity in Ψ1,p,G\Psi_{1,p,G} is the character afforded by the projective cover of the trivial module.
